title: Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, part 6
summary: Part 6 of the career cities series covers 9 career hubs, one sourced fact each; rebuilt 18 Nov 2026 with Hoang's notes (plain title, new creative industries, logos with names in the city scene, paper and flat versions)
changesFromV1: Title is now plain and direct (Hoang, 18 Nov): 'Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, part six.' with a PART 6 pill; no 'Asia, part one', no length
New creative stops (Hoang, 18 Nov: film, anime, game development, cosmetics): Hengdian for film and TV, Seoul for cosmetics, Kyoto for video games, Tokyo for anime

Dropped to stay under 2:00 and keep the map readable: Qingdao and Ulaanbaatar (lead's first picks), Ulsan (a second car stop next to Toyota City) and Yiwu (30 km from Hengdian, so the two pins sat on top of each other)
Voice lines shortened (no job lists); logos with company names appear in the city scene next to Ledger; the fact number counts up
Built in two styles with the same voice and timing: paper (as Parts 4 and 5) and flat

beats.label: title
beats.voice: Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, part six.

beats.label: stop 1 Shenzhen
beats.voice: First, Ledger lands in Shenzhen, China, a hub for tech and electric cars.

beats.label: stop 1 Shenzhen
beats.voice: BYD, based here, sold over 4.6 million vehicles in 2025.

beats.label: stop 2 Jingdezhen
beats.voice: Then, he flies to Jingdezhen, China, a hub for porcelain.

beats.label: stop 2 Jingdezhen
beats.voice: Handmade porcelain here supported over 50,000 jobs in 2025.

beats.label: stop 3 Hengdian
beats.voice: Next, he hops to Hengdian, China, a hub for film and TV.

beats.label: stop 3 Hengdian
beats.voice: In 2025, 4,016 new short-drama crews started filming here.

beats.label: stop 4 Hsinchu
beats.voice: Then, he flies to Hsinchu, Taiwan, a hub for chips.

beats.label: stop 4 Hsinchu
beats.voice: Its science park employed over 177,000 workers in 2024.

beats.label: stop 5 Seoul
beats.voice: Next, he flies to Seoul, South Korea, a hub for cosmetics.

beats.label: stop 5 Seoul
beats.voice: Korea exported 11.4 billion dollars of cosmetics in 2025.

beats.label: stop 6 Kyoto
beats.voice: Then, he lands in Kyoto, Japan, a hub for video games.

beats.label: stop 6 Kyoto
beats.voice: Nintendo, based here, has shipped 26.35 million Switch 2 consoles.

beats.label: stop 7 Sabae
beats.voice: Next, he hops to Sabae, Japan, a hub for eyeglass frames.

beats.label: stop 7 Sabae
beats.voice: Sabae makes about 90 percent of Japan's frames.

beats.label: stop 8 Toyota City
beats.voice: Then, he rides to Toyota City, Japan, a hub for cars.

beats.label: stop 8 Toyota City
beats.voice: Toyota, based here, employs 390,927 people.

beats.label: stop 9 Tokyo
beats.voice: Finally, he lands in Tokyo, Japan, a hub for anime.

beats.label: stop 9 Tokyo
beats.voice: Japan's anime market reached 4.45 trillion yen in 2025.

beats.label: summary
beats.voice: So that was East Asia, from Shenzhen to Tokyo.

beats.label: summary
beats.voice: Next, part seven maps Southeast Asia.

beats.label: cta
beats.voice: To climb in these cities, you need a good business foundation.

beats.label: cta
beats.voice: Go to Edlintics.com to learn technical business skills.

caption:
Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, Part 6, starts in East Asia with nine stops, and each stop shows one industry that city is a hub for, with a sourced fact

So you will meet Shenzhen for tech and electric cars, Jingdezhen for porcelain, Hengdian for film and TV, Hsinchu for chips, Seoul for cosmetics, Kyoto for video games, Sabae for eyeglass frames, Toyota City for cars, and Tokyo for anime

Save the map for later, because Part 7 maps career hub cities across Southeast Asia

maths_check: No sums in the voice. Figures as reported: 4,602,436 vehicles, voiced as 'over 4.6 million' (BYD, 2025); over 50,000 jobs (Jingdezhen handmade porcelain, 2025); 4,016 new short-drama crews (Hengdian, 2025); 177,389 workers, voiced as 'over 177,000' (Hsinchu Science Park, October 2024); USD 11.4 billion (Korea cosmetics exports, 2025); 26.35 million Switch 2 units shipped (Nintendo, to 30 September 2026); about 90% (Sabae's share of Japan's frames); 390,927 employees (Toyota, 31 March 2026); JPY 4.4491 trillion, voiced as '4.45 trillion yen' (AJA, 2025, preliminary). Two currencies appear because each figure stays in the currency it was reported in: US dollars for Korea's exports and yen for Japan's anime market
not_verified: Hengdian's 4,016 are vertical micro-drama (short-drama) crews, not feature films, from a magazine report on Sina; shooting fell sharply in early 2026, so the line is dated 2025. Seoul and Tokyo use country figures (Korea's cosmetics exports, Japan's anime market); Tokyo's figure is AJA's preliminary estimate. Nintendo's figure is units shipped to shops. Hsinchu's worker count is from Wikipedia's Hsinchu Science Park page. LG H&H's 2026 move inside Seoul was not confirmed as finished (both addresses are in Seoul). Hengdian's logo is the Hengdian Group's, the owner of Hengdian World Studios
